snippet.title: STOCKPILE 10 Must-Have Survival Drinks To That NEVER EXPIRE
snippet.description:
Emergency food storage isn't just about canned food and water. Most people overlook the survival drinks that support hydration, energy, immunity, digestion, sleep, and morale during emergencies. In this video, we reveal 10 long-lasting emergency drinks that belong in every prepper pantry.

Here's the thing… storing water alone isn't enough. Your body also needs electrolytes, vitamins, digestive support, and practical nutrition to stay healthy during power outages, natural disasters, or long-term emergencies. From powdered milk tea and electrolyte mixes to chamomile, rose hip tea, coconut water powder, and other shelf-stable essentials, we explain why these overlooked items deserve a place in your emergency supplies.

What most people don't realize is that a well-prepared pantry isn't only about surviving—it's about staying physically and mentally strong when normal life is disrupted. Watch until the end to discover the #1 survival drink that has supported military field operations for generations.

Disclaimer: This video is for educational and informational purposes only. Always follow official emergency preparedness guidelines and consult qualified professionals for medical or nutritional advice.

snippet.title: Emergency Management Minister Eleanor Olszewski highlights Emergency Preparedness Week – May 4, 2026
snippet.description:
Speaking with reporters on Parliament Hill, Emergency Management Minister Eleanor Olszewski highlights Emergency Preparedness Week by encouraging Canadians to make plans and stock supplies for emergency situations. She also announces new emergency response and capacity funding, including $108 million over three years to restart the Humanitarian Workforce Program and $1.93 million for new projects of the Search and Rescue Volunteer Association of Canada (SARVAC).

Minister Olszewski is joined by her parliamentary secretary Anthony Housefather, as well as Conrad Sauvé (president and CEO, Canadian Red Cross), Erik Rowell (director of operations, St. John Ambulance), Mischa Kaplan (CEO, Team Rubicon Canada), and Rick Zelinsky (director of public affairs, The Salvation Army).

snippet.title: Ready, Set, Go Bags! Disaster Preparedness Chikahan with Suzi, Camille, and Iya
snippet.description:
What if may emergency bukas? Prepared ba talaga tayo?

Sa episode na ito, we delve into a very practical but very important topic tungkol sa disaster preparedness.

From go bags, first aid kits, whistles, flashlights, emergency food, water, medicines, and important documents, pinag-usapan natin ang mga basic things na dapat meron at alam ng bawat family.

Pero hindi lang physical supplies ang kailangan.

What happens kung nasa work ka at nasa bahay ang kids? Saan kayo magkikita? Paano kayo magkaka-contact kung mawalan ng signal? Alam ba ng mga bata ang pangalan, number, at address ng parents nila?

Napag-usapan din kung bakit importanteng seryosohin ang earthquake and fire drills. Hindi lang ito paulit-ulit na activity. The goal is to make the response familiar enough na hindi ka na magpa-panic at mag-isip from scratch kapag kailangan na talaga.

At syempre, dahil kami na ’to, hindi mawawala ang random chika.

From emergency whistles na kailangan pa ng tamang angle, to zombie apocalypse scenarios, at mga go bag na prepared… sa cart pa lang, this episode is equal parts useful, eye-opening, and very Mars-coded!

At the end of the day, hindi naman natin gustong mangyari ang mga bagay na pinaghahandaan natin. But being prepared gives you one less thing to worry about when something unexpected happens.

Mars, ikaw? May go bag ka na ba?

When the power goes out, most people think they need an expensive generator or a garage full of survival gear. But for generations, ordinary families lived through blackouts using simple, low-cost methods that still work today.

In this video, you'll discover 10 forgotten blackout tricks that cost almost nothing but can outperform expensive prepper gadgets. From homemade emergency lighting and retained-heat cooking to turning your freezer into a thermal battery and the one survival advantage money can't buy, these practical tips are based on real-world habits that helped people long before modern survival gear existed.

Whether you're preparing for storms, winter outages, hurricanes, or just want to be more self-reliant, these timeless techniques can help you stay safer, warmer, and more comfortable when the grid goes down.

In this video, you'll learn:

How to make an emergency candle from common household items
The bathtub water trick every homeowner should know
How to keep food cold longer during a blackout
Why cheap solar garden lights beat expensive lanterns
How your car can become an emergency power source
The one-room heating strategy used for generations
DIY cooking methods that save precious fuel
Why knowing your neighbors is the ultimate survival tool
